title: AI Factory onion V2: API-2-Pipelines
summary: In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: {api_range} in the API, {pipeline_range} in the pipeline.

evidence.R1: Verified 2026-10-31 23:45 CET for the aif-138 end-to-end run through the ESAF facade (consumer repository jostrm/azure-enterprise-scale-byor-138): catalog jobs in the Factory API's catalog-operations.sqlite and gh run list. API time = the catalog job's created_at to the GitHub run's createdAt. Job total = the job's created_at to updated_at. The jobs' pipeline_runs confirm which run belongs to which job.
evidence.R2: Not in the table: two failed attempts with the same 13 s API time, project 002 deploy 6a380c35 (run 41172892614 failed after 59.6 min) and delete 3bd1d25d (run 41194343416 failed after 24.9 min).
evidence.R3: Scenario 5 (esaf.delete_scale_set, worker route) was blocked when the 2026-10-31 table was verified: four attempts were refused at prepare after about 5 min. After the ownership fixes, attempt m succeeded (update 2026-11-01 16:00 CET): job db2fa13d 15:13-15:24Z, prepare 148 s, then the deletion worker on the API host for about 9 min (no GitHub run), 11.5 min in total. Attempt i (2026-11-01, 91 min, stopped after deleting common-002) is not in the table.

colors.note: Purple is the AI Factory color, which always means the best, so the onion does not use it.
colors.basis: average time in the layer per measured run

consumer.label: Consumer
consumer.name: Consumer: Python with the ESAF facade
consumer.where: A Python session next to the Factory API (the aif-138 walkthrough), or the lifecycle Azure Function
consumer.what: Calls one ESAF scenario method. Calling it is the approval; it gets a job handle back at once.
consumer.called_by: A developer, a notebook or an automation.
consumer.calls: L1: the esaf facade in the azurefactory Python package.

layers.label: L1
layers.name: Clients
layers.ring_top: L1 · CLIENTS · ESAF FACADE · SDK · CLI
layers.where: azurefactory Python package: esaf facade over AzureFactoryClient (purple environment_setup/azurefactory-cli) · CLI · Tkinter wizard (pink) · MAUI ConfigWizard
layers.what: Thin clients. The esaf facade prepares the review, checks it and confirms it in one call, then returns an EsafJob. No deployment logic.
layers.called_by: The consumer: a Python session, a notebook or the lifecycle Function.
layers.calls: L2 over HTTP on loopback with the API key in X-API-Key.

layers.label: L2
layers.name: Factory REST API
layers.where: jostrm/azure-aifactory-config: src/onion_mode.py, src/creation_project_pipeline.py, src/catalog_runtime.py · loopback on the API host
layers.what: Owns every decision: catalog, reviews, consent. For PROJECT it only writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's pipeline: {api_range} before the run starts.
layers.called_by: L1 clients on the same host (catalog and deployment routes accept loopback clients only).
layers.calls: L3: installs infra-project.yml and infra-project-phase.yml in the consumer repository when they are missing or differ, hands the project's variables.json to the run as an environment secret (never committed, deleted after the run), then starts the run.

layers.label: L3
layers.name: Pipelines
layers.where: Consumer repository .github/workflows/infra-project.yml + infra-project-phase.yml, from purple environment_setup/aifactory/bicep/copy_to_local_settings/github-actions · self-hosted runner
layers.what: Does the work: networking and services, then AI Foundry, as separate az deployment steps. {pipeline_range} per PROJECT run, one wall clock for L3, L4 and L5.
layers.called_by: L2 starts the run (GitHub Actions; the Azure DevOps route is not available yet in this mode).
layers.calls: L4: az deployment of the project Bicep and the pipeline-called scripts.

layers.label: L4
layers.name: Bicep + pipeline-called scripts
layers.where: purple environment_setup/aifactory/bicep (esml-genai-1: 31-network, 01-foundation ... 11-integration) and bicep/scripts, at the pinned purple commit
layers.what: Infrastructure as code the pipeline deploys, plus the scripts it runs around it. Its time is inside the pipeline's wall clock.
layers.called_by: L3 pipelines on the self-hosted runner.
layers.calls: L5: resource-group deployments and az CLI calls.

layers.label: L5
layers.name: Azure Resource Manager
layers.where: management.azure.com: deployments, resource groups, resources, role assignments
layers.what: The only layer that changes Azure: networks, private endpoints, DNS, AI Foundry. Its time is inside the pipeline's wall clock.
layers.calls: Nothing in AI Factory: Azure resource providers.

paths.label: PROJECT path (API-2-Pipelines)
paths.text: Consumer > L1 esaf > L2 writes the configuration and starts the run ({api_range}) > L3 infra-project pipeline > L4 Bicep > L5 ({pipeline_range})

paths.label: Worker path (scale-set enroll)
paths.text: L2 freezes a deployment plan ({worker_api}) > L3 factory-lifecycle worker > L4 Bicep > L5 ({worker_pipeline})

steps.title: Same five layers. The API now hands off in seconds.
steps.explanation: In PROJECT mode (onion-deployment-mode API-2-Pipelines) the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline. The pipeline does the work. The colours show where the time goes: green is fast, red is the slowest.
steps.key: API: {api_range} before the pipeline starts. Pipeline: {pipeline_range}.

steps.title: One ESAF call is the approval.
steps.explanation: esaf.upsert_project("002", scale_set="002") prepares the review, checks it and confirms it, then returns an EsafJob at once. The client holds no deployment logic.
steps.key: Fire and forget: job.wait() follows the server-side job to its end.

links.label: prepare + confirm over REST with X-API-Key

steps.title: The API writes the configuration and starts the run.
steps.explanation: It installs infra-project.yml when it is missing or differs, hands the project's variables.json to the run as an environment secret, and starts the run. It no longer freezes an ARM plan or deploys anything itself.
steps.key: Job created to GitHub run created: {api_range} (measured 2026-10-31).

steps.title: The pipeline does the work.
steps.explanation: infra-project.yml calls infra-project-phase.yml for networking and services, then AI Foundry, as separate az deployment steps on the factory's runner. Bicep and ARM time are inside the pipeline's wall clock.
steps.key: Pipeline wall clock: {pipeline_range} per PROJECT run.

links.label: az deployment of the project Bicep

steps.title: The worker route still prepares first.
steps.explanation: Enrolling a scale set takes the factory-lifecycle worker route: the API freezes a deployment plan before it starts the pipeline, and the worker deploys that plan.
steps.key: Worker route: {worker_api} in the API before the pipeline, then {worker_pipeline} in it.

links.label: frozen plan, then start the factory-lifecycle pipeline
the worker deploys the frozen plan's Bicep

steps.title: Seconds in the API, minutes in the pipeline.
steps.explanation: Measured on aif-138 from 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-01. Scenario 6 (delete the factory) is not yet measured.
